blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights the foundational work on transaction management in distributed database systems presented in Mohan et al.'s 1986 paper. The blog post focuses on the core Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol, which ensures atomicity in distributed transactions despite site or communication failures. Colyer emphasizes the protocol's two phases (prepare and commit), the roles of coordinator and subordinates, and the critical logging requirements to guarantee recovery and atomicity. He also notes the paper's emphasis on performance aspects, particularly logging and communication overhead in failure-free scenarios. The post sets the stage for discussing optimizations like Presumed Abort and Presumed Commit in subsequent entries.
paper_title: Transaction Management in the R* Distributed Database Management System
paper_abstract:
Transaction Management in the R*
Distributed Database Management System
C. MOHAN, B. LINDSAY, and R. OBERMARCK
IBM Almaden Research Center

This paper deals with the transaction management aspects of the R* distributed database system. It
concentrates primarily on the description of the R* commit protocols, Presumed Abort (PA) and
Presumed Commit (PC). PA and PC are extensions of the well-known,
two-phase (2P) commit
